site.name: booking
site.summary: booking-clone Clone of the Booking.com hotel booking funnel (home → city list → area filters → detail → room → booking → confirmation), plus other business-line and supporting pages. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: search bar (destination / check-in & out dates / guests), recommended destinations, recent searches, Genius membership prompt, business-line entries in the footer | | `tokyo.html` | Tokyo hotel list: left filter panel (price, stars, rating, amenities, area), right-hand hotel cards (price, rating, review count, distance, free-cancellation tag), sort bar, map entry | | `shinjuku.html` | Shinjuku-area hotel list, same structure as above, pre-filtered to Shinjuku |

run_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full booking system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will start by walking through the core hotel booking funnel from the homepage to confirmation, ensuring data passes correctly between steps. It will then evaluate the adjacent travel verticals (flights, cars, attractions, taxis) and user account management pages (trips, login, support). Finally, it will validate mobile responsiveness, paying special attention to the numerous small tap targets identified in the prescan.
assumptions: The site relies heavily on static HTML files to simulate the booking flow, so navigation will likely follow hardcoded links (e.g., clicking a Tokyo hotel goes to hotel-detail.html).
Filter inputs on search result pages might not dynamically update the DOM, but their state and layout should still be verified.
The 'small_tap_target' warnings indicate a risk for mobile usability, particularly in the top navigation and search bars.
risk_hotspots: Form validation and layout on the main checkout page (reservation.html)
Usability of the complex filter panel on search result pages (tokyo.html, shinjuku.html)
Tap target sizes in the primary navigation header across all pages
Date and guest picker inputs in the primary search bars

phases.title: Core Booking Funnel
phases.objective: Traverse the primary user journey from homepage search to booking confirmation.
key_checks: Interact with the main search bar on index.html
Click through a hotel listing on tokyo.html
Select a room and proceed to checkout
Fill out required fields in reservation.html and submit
exit_criteria: Successfully reached confirmation.html with a simulated booked state.

phases.title: Discovery & Evaluation Features
phases.objective: Validate hotel filtering, sorting, and review reading experiences.
key_checks: Toggle various budget, star rating, and neighbourhood filters on shinjuku.html
Navigate to hotel reviews and interact with review sorting/filtering options
exit_criteria: Filter checkboxes and review sort dropdowns have been interacted with.

phases.title: Adjacent Travel Verticals
phases.objective: Verify the layout and primary search inputs for other business lines.
key_checks: Interact with flight type selectors (Round trip, One way)
Fill out pick-up/drop-off locations for cars and taxis
Check search button triggers across all vertical pages
exit_criteria: All four vertical pages visited and their primary search forms exercised.

phases.title: Account, Support & Marketing
phases.objective: Ensure user account pages, trip management, and informational pages render correctly.
key_checks: Attempt form entry on login/register pages
Interact with trip management actions (Cancel booking, Modify dates) on my-trips.html
Use the search input on the help.html page
exit_criteria: Trip management actions and authentication forms have been evaluated.

phases.title: Mobile Usability Validation
phases.objective: Re-evaluate critical paths on mobile viewport to assess tap targets and responsive layout.
key_checks: Check top navigation menu accessibility on mobile
Verify if filter sidebars stack or collapse on tokyo.html
Ensure form inputs on reservation.html are usable on small screens
exit_criteria: Mobile-specific screenshots captured for the homepage, search results, and checkout form.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 19 HTML pages identified in the prescan.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the primary search form, checkout form, and search filters.
coverage_targets.mobile: Test index.html, tokyo.html, and reservation.html specifically for mobile tap target and layout issues.

notes: Given the high step count limit (80), the agent should have ample time to fill out forms fully before proceeding.
Missing input labels were flagged on several pages (attractions, car-rentals); ensure these are evaluated for accessibility impact.

observation.title: Park Hyatt Tokyo - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions Airport taxis JPY List your property Sign in Home > Japan > Tokyo > Shinjuku > Park Hyatt Tokyo ← Back to results ★★★★★ Park Hyatt Tokyo 📍 3-7-1-2 Nishi Shinjuku, Shinjuku, Tokyo, 163-1055, Japan · Excellent location — rated 9.6/10 🏯 🛌 🍵 🏊 🌄 About Park Hyatt Tokyo Occupying the top 14 floors of the 52-story Shinjuku Park Tower, Park Hyatt Tokyo offers panoramic views of the city skyline and Mount Fuji. The hotel features the renowned New York Grill restaurant, a 20-meter indoor swimming pool, and the Club on the Park fitness center with a stunning view of the city. Each room is spacious and elegantly designed with floor-to-ceiling windows, deep soaking tubs, and original artwork. The hotel is located in the Nishi-Shinjuku business district, a 12-minute walk from Shinjuku Station. Guests can enjoy the Girandole restaurant for all-day dining, the Peak Bar for cocktails with a view, and the Kozue restaurant for authentic Japanese cuisine. The spa offers a range of treatments in a serene setting on the 45th floor. Each room is thoughtfully designed with comfortable bedding, free WiFi, and modern amenities. observation.title: Park Hyatt Tokyo - Guest Reviews - Booking.com
observation.visible_text: Booking.com Stays Flights Car rentals Attractions JPY Sign in Home > Tokyo > Park Hyatt Tokyo > Guest reviews Guest reviews Park Hyatt Tokyo 9.4 Exceptional 3,847 reviews Staff 9.6 Facilities 9.4 Cleanliness 9.6 Comfort 9.5 Value for money 8.8 Location 9.6 Free WiFi 9.2 Breakfast 9.3 All reviews (3,847) Most relevant Most recent Highest score Lowest score All Couples (1,234) Families (876) Solo travellers (543) Business (1,194) TK Takeshi Japan · Couple · Deluxe King Room · 3 nights 10 Absolutely perfect in every way 👍 Liked The views from the 47th floor were breathtaking. Staff remembered our names from the first interaction. The New York Grill breakfast is worth every yen. Pool area is serene and never crowded. 👎 Disliked Nothing to complain about. Perhaps the walk from Shinjuku station is a bit long in summer heat, but the hotel shuttle solves that. Reviewed: June 2025 SM Sarah M. United States · Solo traveller · Park King Room · 5 nights 9.6 Lost in Translation vibes, but better 👍 Liked The atmosphere is exactly what you'd hope for. The library lounge is perfect for quiet afternoons. Girandole breakfast buffet has incredible variety. The bed is the most comfortable I've ever slept in. 👎 Disliked Price is steep, but you get what you pay for. The gym can get busy in the early morning. Reviewed: May 2025 LW Li Wei China · Family · Deluxe Twin Room · 4 nights 9.2 Excellent for families with older children 👍 Liked Spacious rooms, impeccable service. The concierge helped us plan our entire Tokyo itinerary. Kids loved the pool. Location is quiet but still accessible to everything. 👎 Disliked Not many kid-specific amenities. The restaurant dress code made dinner with teenagers a bit formal. Would appreciate a kids' menu. Reviewed: April 2025 JB James B. United Kingdom · Business · Park Suite · 2 nights 9.8 The gold standard for business travel 👍 Liked The suite is extraordinary — separate living area, stunning views, and the bathroom alone is larger than most Tokyo hotel rooms. Club lounge access made early mornings productive. Flawless check-in process. 👎 Disliked Honestly nothing. If I had to nitpick, the in-room coffee machine could be upgraded to a proper espresso machine at this price point. Reviewed: March 2025 YK Yuki K. Japan · Couple · Deluxe King Room · 1 night 8.8 Anniversary celebration done right 👍 Liked They arranged a beautiful cake and champagne for our anniversary without us asking — the concierge noticed it in our booking notes. The Peak Bar at sunset is magical. 👎 Disliked For a one-night stay, the value proposition is harder to justify. The minibar prices are quite high even by luxury hotel standards.
